assistant|battery_health_check_tools: Recommended checking battery health via Windows Battery Report, Mac Battery Health, Coconut Battery, BatteryMon, or HWiNFO
assistant|battery_lifespan_guideline: Most laptop batteries last about 2-3 years; capacity drops to 50-60% after 2-3 years
assistant|battery_disposal_recycling: Advised recycling the old battery via local authorities, manufacturer take-back programs, or retailers like Best Buy, Staples, Office Depot
assistant|battery_disposal_safety: Advised taping battery terminals, never trashing or incinerating lithium-ion batteries
assistant|external_hard_drive_recommenda: Recommended WD My Passport, Seagate Backup Plus, Samsung T5 Portable SSD, LaCie Rugged, and G-Technology G-Drive external drives
assistant|cloud_backup_options: Suggested cloud backup via Google Drive (15GB free), Microsoft OneDrive (5GB free), or Dropbox (2GB free)
assistant|backup_rule_321: Recommended the 3-2-1 backup rule: three copies, two media types, one offsite
assistant|battery_life_software_hardware: Advised lowering screen brightness, disabling unused Bluetooth/Wi-Fi/location services, enabling Power Saver/Low Power Mode, updating the OS, closing resource-intensive apps, cleaning laptop vents, calibrating the battery (drain to 0%, charge to 100%), and updating battery drivers
assistant|battery_charging_habits: Advised charging between 20-80% with a high-quality/genuine charger, avoiding overcharging and extreme temperatures, storing the laptop at ~50% charge in a cool dry place, using a battery-saving browser, disabling unnecessary startup programs, and considering an SSD
assistant|battery_cycle_count_guideline: Most modern laptop batteries are designed to last around 300-500 charge-discharge cycles; a new battery typically retains 80-90% of its capacity after 300-500 cycles
assistant|battery_capacity_timeline: Battery capacity may drop to 70-80% after 1-2 years and to 30-40% after 3-5 years (in addition to 50-60% after 2-3 years)
assistant|battery_lifespan_factors: Battery lifespan depends on age, usage patterns (frequent resource-intensive use degrades it faster), charging habits (frequent deep discharges reduce lifespan), and environmental factors like extreme temperatures and humidity
assistant|battery_physical_inspection: Advised visually inspecting the battery for swelling or bulging (a sign of a faulty battery) and checking that the battery connectors are clean and free of corrosion
assistant|battery_degradation_signs: Signs of battery degradation to look for: capacity significantly lower than original, high cycle count, consistently low voltage, and consistently high temperature
assistant|battery_warranty_check: Recommended checking the laptop's warranty status before replacing the battery, as a valid warranty may cover a free replacement or repair
assistant|battery_disposal_extra_safety: Also advised removing any protective casing before recycling, never crushing or puncturing the battery, and not recycling it with regular electronic waste
